digest.component_or_area: MCP server error handling and CLI consistency
propositions: MCP tool failures currently lack the structured error_envelope discriminator that the CLI emits, forcing agents to pattern-match prose instead of machine codes
The CLI's error codes are scattered across multiple call sites with no central vocabulary source, creating a risk that MCP implements inconsistent or incomplete codes
MCP has two divergent ad-hoc error shapes (_mcp_reads.py explain_criterion and _mcp_llm.py) that must be unified into a single error_envelope format
A single shared classifier error_code_for(exc) in _errors.py must source all three interfaces (library, CLI, MCP) with identical codes drawn from KNOWN_ERROR_CODES
The library interface currently does not expose a machine error discriminator uniformly; RebarError/ConcurrencyError/TrackerRootError do not set .message, requiring str(exc) for the human text field

MCP failures (both exception-raised and returned soft errors) must carry an error code from KNOWN_ERROR_CODES while preserving existing agent-branching signal fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable)
